transcript.content: Hello, I'm glad to meet you. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi doctor. I've been struggling a lot lately with sitting still and constantly fidgeting. I feel like I'm always tapping my hands or feet and squirming in my seat, and it's getting really hard to control.
Have you struggled with this restlessness and fidgeting since your childhood, or is this something that started more recently as an adult?

It's definitely something I've struggled with since I was a kid. I remember always getting in trouble for squirming and tapping my desk in elementary school, well before I was 12, so it isn't a recent thing at all.
Along with this physical restlessness, do you also frequently struggle with paying attention, making careless mistakes, or organizing your tasks?

To be honest, I don't really struggle with paying attention, making careless mistakes, or staying organized. My main issues are definitely more about the physical restlessness and always needing to fidget.
Do you also experience frequent, hard-to-control worry or anxiety about everyday things, or is this physical restlessness mostly independent of worry?
No, I don't really experience frequent or hard-to-control worry or anxiety. This physical restlessness is completely independent of any worry; my body just feels like it always needs to be moving.
Have you ever had distinct periods lasting several days where you felt unusually energetic, needed very little sleep, or had racing thoughts, separate from your usual self?
No, I've never had distinct periods like that where my energy or sleep suddenly changed. My level of restlessness is pretty much the same all the time, and I don't experience racing thoughts.

latest_inference.note: Previously the candidates were [Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Hyperactive/Impulsive Presentation), Bipolar I Disorder, Bipolar II Disorder]. Bipolar I and Bipolar II Disorders are now ruled out because the patient denies any history of distinct periods of abnormally elevated energy, decreased need for sleep, or racing thoughts. This leaves Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Hyperactive/Impulsive Presentation) as the primary diagnosis, consistent with the lifelong history of hyperactivity/impulsivity starting before age 12, without significant inattentive symptoms or anxiety.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient exhibits chronic, lifelong symptoms of physical hyperactivity and impulsivity (fidgeting, tapping, squirming) that began before age 12. They do not report significant inattentive symptoms, ruling out the combined presentation. Other conditions like GAD or bipolar disorder were ruled out based on the absence of excessive worry, episodic mood changes, or decreased need for sleep.
